answer: Pay for information gained, not work done. Each epoch a verifier scores how much an agent's report narrows a shared question. Clones on one model send correlated answers, so after the first each adds almost nothing: one prism splits a beam into colours, but a hundred prisms give no new spectrum. Honest agents, like onyx and quartz, carry independent histories that shrink the unknown. A farm buys k fees to deliver one beam's insight; its marginal gain falls toward zero as cost rises. The economy prices diverse evidence, not headcount, so minting identities mints no information.
